evidence: South Face is class 4 (the standard route): a long class 3/4 scramble on loose 4th-class rock, usually done once snow-free.
note: No source found for the 'occasional low 5th' in the headline.

evidence: Southeast Ridge (Anderson/Kearney 1977): Grade III, class 5.6.
Southwest Ridge listed as class 4.
CJ Couloir (a long snow couloir, icy late season) to the East Ridge, then up to about 1,000 ft of 3rd-4th class rock and heather to the summit.
note: The couloir can be AI2 ice late in the season (ice_grade holds it); in normal conditions the crux is the exposed class 4 ridge rock. The record's breakdown 'low 5th' step was not confirmed by any source.

evidence: Alpine Institute: V, 5.8, AI2 (a short chimney, mostly 5.5, with a couple of 5.8 moves); Mountain Project lists it only as 'Easy 5th' plus snow.
note: Sources disagree; MP gives no number, so the most specific published grade (5.8) is kept. Snow/ice to AI2 near the top.

evidence: The NE Rib is usually done via the 1957 start at V 5.6; the 1951 start is less direct and 'has a scary 5.7 pitch'.
note: Top of the record's 5.6-5.7 range; 5.7 belongs to the 1951 start that names this row, while the popular 1957 variation start is 5.6.

evidence: Mountain Project: Northeast Ridge (1963 Route) 5.7+ with steep snow.
Clean Break IV 5.10b/c, 15 pitches; the pitch-1 splitter is the 5.10c crux.
note: Top of the 5.10b/c slash grade, matching the 5.10c pitch in the record's own breakdown.

evidence: Easiest route is the South Ridge scramble, class 3, with the final scramble Class 3.
Mountain Project: North Face 5.6.
Mountain Project: Koala Krack 5.4.
Mountain Project: Northwest Face 5.7+, 5 pitches.
Mountain Project: South Face 5.8.
Normal route is a class 3/4 scramble up the south side to the Katsuk-Mesahchie col and east ridge; the south gully has a little 4th class for the final 100 ft.
Mountain Project lists Blue Betty at Keechelus Lake Ice as WI3-.
Mountain Project's Kendall Peak area lists Kendall Cliff - North Face as WI3+.
The standard route off the PCT is a class 2 scramble on loose rock; the alternative ridge-top finish is Class 3-4.
South-face route is Class 2+ overall, but the final 250 ft 'will certainly involve some class 4' up one of the ribs or gullies.
From the Klawatti-Austera col, Class 3 scrambling leads to The Smokestack, which is bypassed; the record says Class 4 in spots.
note: Top of the record's own 'Class 3 (Class 4 in spots)'; no source gives a single crux grade.

evidence: South/SE face from Klawatti Col: 45-50° snow through a constriction (icy at times, bergschrund bridges) in early season; later it melts out to slabs with a moat.
note: No source confirms the 5.2 / low-5th in the record's breakdown. In snow condition it is steep snow (Class 3 by the brief); Class 4 is kept for the late-season slabby rock.

fix.rock_grade: Class 4 (slabby rock once the snow melts)

evidence: Mountain Project: SW Buttress 5.3, Grade III; 2-3 short low-5th pitches from the moat, then scrambling.
Kololo Peaks are Class 2 climbs; the White Chuck Glacier route passes a couple of minor Class 2+ cliff bands; the difficulty is glacier travel and approach.
Columbia Glacier route: about 50 ft of loose class 3+ exiting the glacier, a summit block with moat-stemming and some exposed 4th class; other accounts call the final section exposed class 3.
note: Top of the record's Class 3-4; accounts vary between class 3 and 4.

evidence: Quartz Creek Trail to Curry Gap, up the NE ridge across the Pride Glacier, then Class 3 rock on the glacier's left edge to the summit via its SE corner.
East Ridge from La Bohn Gap is a Class 2 route, listed as the easiest on the peak.
identity: The id says 'southwest_slopes' but the route name and overview describe the East Ridge from La Bohn Gap.

evidence: Mountain Project: Bavarian Dark WI5.
Mountain Project: Champagne WI5.
Mountain Project: Guinness WI4-5.
Mountain Project: Rainier Light WI3-4.
Lake Mountain is a class 2 scramble with route finding (no single move needs hands); several gullies of similar difficulty.
Mountain Project: Classic Route 4th class; the easiest route on Lane is class 4 scrambling (steep upper class 3 with a 4th-class finish).
Mountain Project: The Zipper WI2 M2 Steep Snow, Grade II, 3 pitches, about 45°.

evidence: Mountain Project: Lover's Lane AI1 Mod. Snow; the steepest and narrowest of the three couloirs.

evidence: Mountain Project: Lemah Glacier 4th class, Easy Snow; the east-face chute crux is steep snow/ice or rock scrambling, at least Class 3 and some say Class 4.
Goatshead Spire (Goodman/Mason, 1982) is listed with no grade; MP notes that Lemah's summits all have class 4-low 5th routes.
